concept.title: More Unofficial Rules of Marriage
concept.human_truth: Marriage is two imperfect people repeatedly entering each other's tiny problems until every problem becomes ours.
concept.emotional_arc: separate habits -> reciprocal rescue -> synchronized chaos -> belonging
concept.visual_system: One continuous weekend trip, beginning and ending at home. Body distance contracts and actions become increasingly shared.

slides.copy:
More unofficial rules of marriage
that nobody tells you
slides.visual: Friday evening in their bedroom-living-room threshold. A half-packed suitcase is open. Aachu searches through clothes while Zuv crosses the room carrying two mugs and carefully stepping over a charging cable. They occupy different parts of the frame but exchange one familiar glance. The room is mildly unfinished, never dirty or cluttered.
slides.emotion: warm recognition before a shared weekend
slides.pose: High overhead geography: separate actions, readable silhouettes, natural two-inch height relationship.
slides.wardrobe: Continuous travel-weekend wardrobe drawn from the selected identity references: Aachu in a soft light casual top and blue jeans; Zuv in a dark casual shirt and charcoal trousers.
slides.props: One open suitcase, one charging cable, two mugs, a few folded clothes.
slides.background: Warm practical lamp, bed edge, doorway and clean negative space; no portraits, mirrors, readable labels or extra people.
slides.continuity_lock: Exactly two people. Establish separated movement that will become synchronized by slide 9.

slides.copy:
Rule no. 1
“Should we order something?”
is not a question.
The decision has already been made.
slides.visual: Aachu and Zuv sit at opposite ends of the sofa during packing. One performs a casual asking gesture while the other is already selecting dishes on the phone placed between them. Both lean toward the same phone, revealing that the question was ceremonial rather than undecided.
slides.emotion: private conspiracy disguised as a question
slides.pose: Sofa-level medium two-shot; bodies apart, eye-lines and hands converge on the central phone.
slides.props: One phone with abstract food shapes only, no readable UI; suitcase soft in background.
slides.background: Sofa edge and travel preparation traces only; no decorative clutter.
slides.continuity_lock: Exactly two people and one phone. Neither person is framed as the sole impulsive one.

slides.copy:
Rule no. 2
If one person asks, “Kahan hai?”
The other must find it
without being told what “it” is.
slides.visual: During packing, Zuv urgently searches around the suitcase for the room keys while the keys already dangle visibly from the fingers of his raised searching hand. Aachu pauses beside the suitcase and silently points at his hand, familiar rather than mocking.
slides.emotion: exhausted familiarity with a recurring ritual
slides.pose: Deep-focus medium-wide. Zuv foreground searching; Aachu midground pointing; their gaze connects to the keys.
slides.background: Bedroom-to-entryway depth with selected packing traces.
slides.continuity_lock: Exactly two people. The key-holding hand, pointing hand and both owners must be anatomically unambiguous.

slides.copy:
Rule no. 3
Old screenshots
do not have an expiry date.
They can be presented as evidence
at any time.
slides.visual: Zuv confidently gestures that he never said something. Aachu calmly turns her phone toward him with old message evidence already prepared. His free hand freezes mid-defence and his expression collapses into a sheepish smile; she remains composed, not triumphant or hostile.
slides.pose: Over Aachu's shoulder toward Zuv's reaction. Phone foreground, faces and hand reaction readable.
slides.props: One phone showing only abstract message blocks and a faint old date shape, never readable dialogue or invented interface text.
slides.background: Sparse living-room edge with packing continuing behind them.
slides.continuity_lock: Exactly two people and one phone. No aggression, extra hands, reflections or readable phone text.

slides.copy:
Rule no. 4
The person who did not pack
will always ask,
“Charger rakh liya?”
Usually when you’re already in the cab.
slides.visual: Aachu is already seated in the waiting cab with both travel bags stacked beside and across her knees. Zuv, carrying only his phone, leans through the open cab door and asks with casual late confidence. Aachu slowly turns toward him with a dry, disbelieving look; he realizes the timing and gives a sheepish half-smile. No charger appears anywhere. The joke is carried by luggage ownership, timing and reaction.
slides.emotion: the exact second casual confidence meets affectionate disbelief
slides.pose: Aachu sits inside the cab with both bags clearly hers; Zuv leans in empty-handed except for his phone. Their gaze connects across the open cab door.
slides.wardrobe: Same clothes with light travel layers drawn from identity references.
slides.props: One cab, two travel bags owned by Aachu, and Zuv's phone. No charger or socket is visible.
slides.background: Minimal cab interior and open rear door; no driver, pedestrians, reflections, home doorway or background figures.
slides.continuity_lock: Exactly two people. Aachu and both bags are inside the cab; Zuv leans in carrying no luggage. No charger appears. Keep the couple entirely in the lower 42 percent of the canvas so the exact five-line copy has a wide, airy upper field.

slides.copy:
Rule no. 5
Wi-Fi starts working
the moment your spouse enters the room.
Nobody knows why.
slides.visual: Inside the hotel, Aachu crouches near a router after trying every fix. Zuv casually enters through the bathroom doorway doing nothing. At that exact moment the router's lights become steady and the nearby laptop changes from a disconnected symbol to a simple connected symbol. Aachu slowly looks up at him, personally betrayed by technology; he gives a helpless shrug.
slides.pose: Low medium from router height. Aachu active in foreground, Zuv relaxed in doorway, strong eye-line reversal.
slides.wardrobe: Same weekend wardrobe, relaxed after travel.
slides.props: One router, one continuous cable, one laptop with a simple non-branded connectivity symbol.
slides.background: Hotel desk and bathroom doorway, restrained and unbranded.
slides.continuity_lock: Exactly two people. Router cable and socket must be physically coherent; no mirrors, reflections or readable UI.

slides.copy:
Rule no. 6
Midnight hunger
is never one person’s emergency.
The entire house gets activated.
slides.visual: Blue hotel night after one person admits hunger. Show the consequence rather than the whisper: both are fully activated. Aachu sits forward comparing food options while Zuv pulls on slippers and empties their remaining snack bag onto the bed between them. Their separate tasks form one shared operation.
slides.pose: High overhead wide echoing slide 1, but their bodies now angle toward the same central task.
slides.wardrobe: Tasteful relaxed night layers derived from the identity references; no caricatured sleepwear.
slides.props: One phone with abstract food shapes, one small snack bag, two slippers, disrupted blanket.
slides.background: Hotel bed under one warm bedside lamp within cool blue night.
slides.continuity_lock: Exactly two people. No delivery person, background figure, extra phones or readable packaging.

slides.copy:
Rule no. 7
Every unnecessary purchase
begins immediately after
a serious conversation
about saving money.
slides.visual: The next afternoon, Aachu and Zuv leave a local market carrying one beautiful but obviously impractical oversized lamp together. A folded budget note sticks harmlessly from a pocket. Both look from the object to each other with equal guilt and delight; the purchase physically requires their cooperation.
slides.pose: Street-level moving wide. Both hands support different ends of the same object; shoulder distance is close.
slides.wardrobe: Same weekend wardrobe with story-supported travel layers.
slides.props: One oversized unbranded lamp and one folded paper with no readable writing.
slides.background: Minimal market threshold with no vendors, crowd, signage, portraits or readable labels.
slides.continuity_lock: Exactly two people. Both are equally responsible; the lamp has plausible weight and four traceable supporting hands.

slides.copy:
Rule no. 8
Nobody is actually in charge.
Both just keep showing up.
Usually saying, “Maine bola tha.”
slides.visual: Back home, Aachu and Zuv try to carry the travel bags and oversized lamp through the doorway together. The lamp begins to slip; both catch and stabilize it in the same instant. Once safe, each points lightly at the other with a free finger and they break into laughter, shoulder-to-shoulder. This returns to slide 1's home geography, but now their movement is synchronized and the shared object connects them.
slides.pose: Lower, closer doorway view. Their bodies overlap centrally; the simultaneous catch is the primary action and the mirrored accusation is the reaction.
slides.wardrobe: Same continuous weekend wardrobe, slightly rumpled from travel.
slides.props: The same oversized lamp, two travel bags and the coiled recovered charger visible in an outer pocket.
slides.background: Warm home light, doorway and quiet traces from slide 1; generous upper-middle text space.
slides.continuity_lock: Exactly two people. Both participate in catching the lamp; no anonymous hands, reflections, bystanders or duplicated objects.

copy.caption_recommended: Marriage is not one person having all the answers. It is two people repeatedly entering each other’s tiny problems until every problem becomes ours. The charger gets forgotten, the screenshots survive, the budget loses—and somehow, both people still show up. Usually saying, “Maine bola tha.” Send this to the person who joins every unnecessary emergency.
